headline: Your Optiwise waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing Walmart 1P suppliers and 3P marketplace brands into the right Optiwise listing, Rich Media, and ads offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Ritesh Jhamnani.
productSummary: Optiwise.ai is an Algorithm Optimization Platform (AOP) for Walmart 1P suppliers and 3P marketplace sellers: Gen-AI listing optimization (Item Spec 5.0 compliance, keyword-rich titles/descriptions, Amazon-to-Walmart import), Rich Media / BTF (Enhanced Brand Content) that transforms Amazon A+ 100x faster, TACoS-driven sponsored ads, seasonality, growth recommendations, and Olivia, a Gen-AI assistant watching 78 catalog and ads signals. Homepage line: expand Amazon success to Walmart. Enterprise page: not a PIM like Salsify or Syndigo. Named proof on optiwise.ai: 1,000+ brands, 20M+ products optimized across Walmart.com and Amazon, 470+ categories, 12+ years of Walmart partnership / Walmart Connect partner, founded by ex-Walmart and ex-Amazon tech leaders who optimized Walmart listings for 8 years. Measured outcomes on /enterprise/: 2.8x increase in digital pen, 60% digital sales growth, 18% content-quality-score improvement, 47% ROAS lift; average brand has 3,000 backend issues, 2,100 digital-shelf issues, 55 Omni Spec 5.0 issues, 161 backend attribute issues; fixing frontend issues averages +20% digital sales, backend +40%. Homepage sample data: 35-40% cost saved vs manual optimization. On-site testimonials: Jonathan Feldman 212% 3P / 300% 1P in three quarters; Claudia L Borunda 3X product sales; Nick 121% revenue; Acquco (Lucas Millman) doubled YoY with v5 item-spec compliance. Case studies: content score 86% and Walmart listing score 82% in 3 months; EBC 2.5x revenue in one month (90+ min per EBC to <1 min). Pricing on /pricing/: free plan, 3P from $249/mo, 1P from $999/mo, managed services custom. Free Chrome extension. Free backend audit CTA on /enterprise/.
coreInsight: Ritesh already sells Walmart listing, SEO, and ads optimization so 1P suppliers and 3P brands stop paying for traffic that a broken catalog cannot convert. The one list is in-TAM Walmart sellers plus Amazon brands expanding to Walmart. The one routing signal is how the catalog already shows up. Category labels are merge tags after routing, not a second waterfall.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is how the catalog already shows up
sections.takeaway: A Walmart PDP plus Amazon PDP already names live ads or a listing/ads/PIM competitor, Amazon A+ with no Walmart BTF, a thin Walmart listing, or none of those. That catalog-state is stronger than a title guess, and it is free to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every Walmart 1P supplier and 3P marketplace brand
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Ads or a named competitor goes first, then Amazon A+ with no Walmart BTF, then a thin Walmart PDP, then every remaining in-TAM seller.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each catalog-state gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Ads or a competitor gets an Algorithm Switch Brief. Amazon A+ with no Walmart BTF gets an A+ to Walmart BTF Brief. A thin Walmart PDP gets a Spec 5.0 Listing Score Brief. The rest get the Digital Pen Playbook.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Switch the ads stack, port A+ to Walmart BTF, raise the listing score, then cover the rest
sections.takeaway: The list is always in-TAM Walmart 1P suppliers and 3P marketplace brands plus Amazon brands expanding to Walmart, aimed at e-commerce, marketplace, and channel titles. Category is a merge tag, not a second TAM. A/Bs sit on the exclusive routes.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the catalog state already on their listings
sections.takeaway: Notice the ads stack, the Amazon A+, or the thin Walmart PDP, poke the traffic-that-cannot-convert gap that catalog-state implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the ads-or-competitor route first
sections.takeaway: Start where they already pay for Walmart traffic or a listing/ads tool and a broken catalog still cannot convert the click. Prove reply density, then roll A+-with-no-BTF, thin-PDP, and the remaining-TAM catch-all.

signalReasons: LinkedIn plus Walmart seller and Amazon-brand directories are the TAM Ritesh already named: Walmart 1P suppliers and 3P marketplace brands, plus Amazon brands expanding to Walmart.

The same Walmart PDP plus Amazon PDP scrape returns live ads or a named listing/ads/PIM competitor (Salsify or Syndigo on optiwise.ai/enterprise, or a Walmart ads platform), Amazon A+ with no Walmart BTF / Rich Media / EBC, or a thin Walmart listing, which is enough to route without a second enrichment product.

The ladder maps to live Optiwise positioning: Algorithm Optimization Platform (not a PIM like Salsify or Syndigo); Gen-AI listing optimization and Item Spec 5.0; Rich Media / BTF that transforms Amazon A+ 100x faster; TACoS-driven sponsored ads; Olivia watching 78 catalog and ads signals; 1,000+ brands, 20M+ products, 2.8x digital pen (all on optiwise.ai / enterprise).
Category labels are scrape filters and merge tags. They are not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last, never the TAM spine.

launchPlan: Confirm in_tam definition: Walmart 1P suppliers and 3P marketplace brands, plus Amazon brands expanding to Walmart (Optiwise buyer set on optiwise.ai).

Pull Sales Nav for those companies, then scrape Walmart and Amazon PDPs plus BuiltWith for catalog_state. Suppress known Optiwise customers when the signal is visible. Named testimonials on optiwise.ai are not a blanket exclude.
Launch Tier 1 only until reply density is clear (target ~1 positive / 150-300).
Add Tier 2 amazon_aplus_no_walmart_btf once Tier 1 copy is stable.
Add Tier 3 walmart_thin_pdp, then the catch-all for remaining in-TAM sellers.
Enrich emails via Apollo only after the account is routed.

A/B Algorithm Switch Brief vs 2.8x digital-pen / 47% ROAS proof on Tier 1 before cloning to lower tiers. Do not invent proof numbers that are not on optiwise.ai. Category is a merge tag, not a second waterfall. Tier shares are estimated and flagged.
